title: Add fractions with different denominators
transcript:
How do you add two thirds and one fourth?

Each full strip is one whole. The wholes must be the same size.

The bottom number tells how many equal pieces make a whole. The top counts the pieces we have.

Thirds and fourths are different sizes. First, make the pieces the same size.

Multiply the bottom numbers: three times four is twelve.

Split each third into four. Multiply both numbers by four: two thirds becomes eight twelfths.

Split each fourth into three. Multiply both numbers by three: one fourth becomes three twelfths.

Neither amount has changed. We have only divided it into smaller pieces.

Now combine eight twelfths and three twelfths: eleven twelfths.

Add the top numbers. Keep twelve on the bottom, because the pieces are still twelfths.

That shared bottom number is called a common denominator.

Finally, simplify if you can divide the top and bottom evenly by the same whole number greater than one. Eleven and twelve have no such number, so eleven twelfths is our answer.
